properties.summary: Forty acres, an existing 1,800-square-foot mobile home, a 30x60 barn, reported high-and-dry usable land, and a recent $55,000 price cut make this a strong operational base rather than raw dirt. The big question is whether Madison County will support Joe's intended commercial use and whether the existing infrastructure can be reused economically.

confirmed: Current listing price is $295,000 after a $55,000 reduction from $350,000.
The parcel is 40.02 acres in Madison County, about six miles from I-10 according to the listing.
A 1,800-square-foot manufactured home and 30x60 barn are reported onsite.
The listing reports a well, county-road frontage and high-and-dry usable acreage.
The manufactured home is tenant occupied and the broker states it needs extensive work.
unknowns: What exact zoning and future-land-use designations apply to parcel 24-2S-10-1473-004-000?
Can an RV park, campground, cabins, events or other revenue-producing uses be approved here?
What septic system exists and what commercial wastewater capacity is feasible?
Are the barn, home, well, septic and electrical improvements permitted and reusable?
How much of the advertised high-and-dry claim survives FEMA, wetlands, soils and drainage review?
dealKillers: County land-use rules block the intended revenue model.
Wastewater limitations prevent a viable site count.
Existing improvements require enough remediation that their head start disappears.
Flood, wetlands, access or road conditions materially reduce usable acreage or guest access.
nextActions: Pull Madison County GIS, zoning, future land use, FEMA flood, wetlands and soils for parcel 24-2S-10-1473-004-000.
Ask Madison County planning for the written approval path for campground/RV/cabin/event uses on this parcel.
Verify permits and condition for the home, 30x60 barn, well, septic and electrical service, including tenant status and possession at closing.

properties.locationAccuracy: Listing coordinates; parcel boundaries and shoreline require GIS verification
properties.zoning: Agricultural reported by listing; exact Volusia County zoning and future land use require parcel-level verification
properties.waterfront: Extensive Shaw Lake frontage and a natural spring reported
properties.floodZone: Unknown; listing identifies wetlands on the parcel and describes the existing home as high and dry
properties.utilities: Public water reported plus two power supplies and two septic systems; capacity and permits require verification
properties.moneyToday: NOT YET — PREMIUM PRICE, PREMIUM DESTINATION STORY
properties.summary: This is one of the strongest destination-oriented raw-property leads on the board: 40 acres with private Shaw Lake frontage, a reported natural spring, an existing 2-bedroom home, two septic systems and two power supplies, plus a $100,000 price reduction. It costs materially more than the Madison County candidates, but the waterfront and springs corridor create a guest draw they do not have. Wetlands, floodplain, shoreline constraints and commercial entitlement are the deciding issues.

confirmed: Multiple current listing sources show 40 acres at $500,000 after a July 2026 reduction from $600,000.
The property is marketed with extensive Shaw Lake frontage and a natural spring.
A 1,072-square-foot 2-bedroom, 1-bath home built in 1938 is included and sold as-is.
The listing reports two power supplies and two septic systems; Zillow also reports electric utility service on the property.
The parcel is APN 4835-00-00-0430 and listings describe it as agricultural with wetlands and potential subdivision subject to approvals.

Volusia County records show that temporary campsites and recreational uses have previously been processed through special exceptions on A-1 agricultural land, demonstrating that a discretionary approval path can exist, but not that this parcel qualifies.
unknowns: What exact zoning and Future Land Use designation apply to APN 4835-00-00-0430, and is the parcel inside the City of Pierson or unincorporated Volusia County jurisdiction?
How much of the 40 acres is wetlands, floodplain, shoreline buffer or otherwise unavailable for RV sites, cabins, roads and wastewater?

Can a permanent campground/RV park, cabins, event use or mixed lodging concept be approved, and would it require rezoning, special exception, comprehensive-plan amendment or other discretionary approval?
What are the permitted capacities and condition of both septic systems and both electrical services, and can public water serve commercial demand?
What shoreline, dock, stormwater and environmental permits would be required for guest access to Shaw Lake and the natural spring?
Is practical large-RV ingress/egress available from N Pine Street without major road or entrance work?
dealKillers: Wetlands, floodplain or environmental buffers leave too little contiguous usable acreage for a viable site plan.
Commercial transient lodging or campground use cannot be approved under the parcel's zoning and Future Land Use framework.
Wastewater expansion is infeasible or prohibitively expensive because of soils, lake setbacks or environmental rules.
Large-RV access, commercial entrance requirements or neighborhood compatibility make operations impractical.
The waterfront and spring cannot be used meaningfully by guests, leaving the $500,000 acquisition premium unsupported.
nextActions: Use Volusia County ConnectLive/GRM mapping and the property appraiser to confirm jurisdiction, zoning, Future Land Use, overlays, parcel boundaries and permit history for APN 4835-00-00-0430.
Map FEMA floodplain, wetlands, soils and shoreline/environmental buffers and estimate contiguous dry usable acreage before spending money on design work.

Request a pre-application conversation with Volusia County or Pierson planning, as applicable, specifically for a permanent RV park/campground, cabins and event uses; ask what discretionary approvals would be required.
Pull permits and inspect both septic systems, both electrical services, public-water availability and the 1938 house before assigning value to existing infrastructure.
Confirm commercial driveway geometry and large-RV turning access from N Pine Street, then sketch a conservative site count using only verified dry acreage.
